## Purpose

Try to use MOM6 data to calculate subsurface heatwaves in the California Current, taking advantage of the new earthmover setup for data access.

## Import Data

```{r setup,include=F}
# Lazily load the entire dataset
library(rnaturalearth)
library(ncdf4)
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(scales)
library(terra)
library(here)
library(tidyterra)
library(viridis)
library(colorspace)
library(tictoc)

theme_set(theme_minimal()+theme(panel.border = element_rect(color='black',fill=NA)))
```

Here is the URL for the monthly earthmover hindcast

```{r}
url <- "https://compute.earthmover.io/v1/services/dap2/NOAA-PMEL/cefi-nep-hindcast-monthly/main/regrid/main/opendap"
ds <- nc_open(url)
```

## Metadata

Calculate some useful reference tables for the dataset and set our study area

```{r lookups}
# variable names as a table with definitions
vardefs <- map(names(ds$var),\(x){
  ncatt_get(ds,x) |> 
    as_tibble() |> 
    mutate(varname=x)
}) |> bind_rows()
# ncdf dimensions as a list of indexed lookup tables
dims <- imap(ds$dim, \(x,n){
  tibble(value=c(x$vals),name=n,units=x$units) |> 
    mutate(index=row_number())
}) |> set_names(names(ds$dim))

# time index
timetbl <- dims$time |> 
  mutate(date=as.Date(value,origin="1993-01-01")) |> 
  mutate(month=month(date),year=year(date))
range(timetbl$date)
print(paste(nrow(timetbl),"months of data."))

# depths for each layer
dims$z_l |> 
  ggplot(aes(index,value))+geom_col()+
  labs(x="depth layer",y="depth (m)")
# grabbing the first 36 depth layers gets us down to 1000m
```
## Define US EEZ

We want to restrict our study area to the US EEZ.

```{r}
eez <- read_sf(here('data','us_west_coast_eez.shp'))

st_bbox(eez)

```

Define the study box and make a template raster extent.

```{r domain}
# define a study area bounding box
latmin <- 32
latmax <- 48.5
lonmin <- 230
lonmax <- 244

# indices
lons <- dims$lon |> filter(value >= lonmin, value <= lonmax)
lats <- dims$lat |> filter(value >= latmin, value <= latmax)
# subsets of lats/lons
lon_sub <- pull(lons,value)
lat_sub <- pull(lats,value)
# indexes
lon_idx <-  pull(lons,index)
lat_idx <- pull(lats,index)
# counts
lon_count <- length(lon_sub)
lat_count=length(lat_sub)

# a raster extent covering this box, for later plotting
rext <- ext(min(lon_sub), max(lon_sub), min(lat_sub), max(lat_sub))
```

## Choosing Isopycnals

Because pressure/density at depth can obfuscate some effects of changing temperatures, we want to try to track these heatwaves along isopycnals, that is, surfaces of common density. For now, we need to decide on a common subsurface isopycnal. Later, we can try our calculations for other isopycnals.

MOM6 has a potential density variable:

```{r}
vardefs[grepl("density",vardefs$long_name),]
```
Let's extract some density data and look for common isopycnals. This function extracts one time-step from the given ncdf, but extracts data across all `min_zind:max_zind` depth indices.

```{r}
get_3Dslice <- function(ncurl=url,varname,tidx,min_zind=1,max_zind=36){
  nc <- nc_open(ncurl)
  tic("pulling variable")
  out <- ncvar_get(
    nc,
    varid=varname,
    # xyzt (time is last dimension)
    start=c(min(lon_idx),min(lat_idx),min_zind,tidx),
    count=c(lon_count,lat_count,length(min_zind:max_zind),1)
  )
  toc()
  nc_close(nc)
  out
}
```

Try this for an arbitrary time slice.

```{r}
test <- get_3Dslice(ncurl=url,varname="thetao",tidx=101)
# find the mean pressure at each depth slice
testprof <- apply(test,3,mean,na.rm=T)
tibble(depth=dims$z_l$value[1:36],density=testprof) |> 
  ggplot(aes(depth,density))+geom_line()+coord_flip()+
  scale_x_reverse()
```

Let's do this for a number of time slices, then find the average density at each depth level (again, just to pick some reasonable isopycnals to track)

```{r}
# set.seed(1234)
# use 2013 as example year
# tsamp <- sample(dims$time$index,size = 20,replace=F)
tsamp <- timetbl |> filter(year==2013) |> pull(index)
testl <- map(tsamp, \(x) get_3Dslice(ncurl=url,varname="rhopot0",tidx=x))
testl <- simplify2array(testl)
# find the mean pressure at each depth slice and month
profmean <- apply(testl,c(3,4),mean,na.rm=T)
profsd <- apply(testl,c(3,4),sd,na.rm=T)
profmin <- apply(testl,c(3,4),min,na.rm=T)
profmax <- apply(testl,c(3,4),max,na.rm=T)
profq95 <-apply(testl,c(3,4),quantile,probs=c(0.95),na.rm=T)
profq05<-apply(testl,c(3,4),quantile,probs=c(0.05),na.rm=T)

profdf <- crossing(month=1:12,
                   depth=dims$z_l$value[1:36]) |> 
  mutate(density=c(profmean),
         sd=c(profsd),
         min=c(profmin),
         max=c(profmax),
         q05=c(profq05),
         q95=c(profq95),
         upr=density+sd,lwr=density-sd) 

profdf |> 
  mutate(month=as.factor(month)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(color=month))+
  scale_color_manual(values=viridis_pal()(12))+
  # geom_ribbon(aes(depth,density,ymin=lwr,ymax=upr),
  #             fill=viridis_pal()(10)[4],col=NA,alpha=0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(depth,density))+
  geom_line(aes(depth,q95),linetype=2)+
  geom_line(aes(depth,q05),linetype=2)+
  coord_flip()+
  scale_x_reverse()
```

For now, choose 1025.5 kg/m^3 and 1026.5 kg/m^3 as our reference isopycnals, often associated with depths between ~50-250m. The other useful thing from this plot is that it suggests we never need to extract data deeper than 250m for this purpose.

```{r}
tgt1 <- 1025.5
tgt2 <- 1026.5
```

## Calculating Isopycnal Temperature

Because the dataset is organized by depth layers (not isopycnals), we need to calculate this in a few steps for each time step in the data:

1. Find the depth layers from a potential density field that most closely match the target density
2. Extract from the temperature field at those depths

The primary bottleneck in the processing is the accessing and downloading of the original data. Without overtaxing my computer, I think we could do the isopycnal calculation on a year of data at a time, rather than by month. This should speed up the overall workflow time because there are fewer unique index calls to the dataset.


```{r}
calc_isopyc_yr <- function(ncurl=url,yr,target_rho=tgt1,min_zind=1,max_zind=24,rast=F){
  
  # find time indices
  ti <- timetbl |> filter(year==yr) |> pull(index)
  tstart <- min(ti)
  tcount <- length(ti)
  tic(paste("Calculating isopycnals for",yr,"starting at index",tstart))
  # get density
  tic(paste("Pulling",length(min_zind:max_zind),"depth slices"))
  
  nc <- nc_open(ncurl)
  
  rhopot <- ncvar_get(
    nc,
    varid="rhopot0",
    # xyzt (time is last dimension)
    start=c(min(lon_idx),min(lat_idx),min_zind,tstart),
    # grab a year of data
    count=c(lon_count,lat_count,length(min_zind:max_zind),tcount)
  )
  toc()
  
  # get temperature
  tic(paste("Pulling",length(min_zind:max_zind),"temperature slices"))
  thetao <- ncvar_get(
    nc,
    varid="thetao",
    # xyzt (time is last dimension)
    start=c(min(lon_idx),min(lat_idx),min_zind,tstart),
    count=c(lon_count,lat_count,length(min_zind:max_zind),tcount)
  )
  toc()
  
  nc_close(nc)
  
  # find which depths are closest to the target density
  # tic("Calculating isopycnal")
  rhodiff <- abs(rhopot-target_rho)
  # rhodiff[rhodiff>0.2] <- NA
  # 
  # # how many depth layers are within 0.2 density units?
  # test <- apply(rhodiff,c(1,2,4), function(x) {
  #   sum(!is.na(x))
  # })
  
  rhowhich <- apply(rhodiff,c(1,2,4), function(x) {
    ifelse(!all(is.na(x)), which.min(x), NA_integer_)
  })
  
  # extract temperature at those depths
  dvals <- dims$z_l$value[min_zind:max_zind]
  tic("Extracting temperature along isopycnal")
  nt <- dim(rhopot)[4] # times (should be 12 months in a year)
  ni <- dim(rhopot)[1] # lons
  nj <- dim(rhopot)[2] # lats
  
  # arrays to hold temperature (d) and depth (z) of isopycnal
  d <- array(NA,dim=c(ni,nj,nt))
  z <- array(NA,dim=c(ni,nj,nt))
  
  # for every month
  for (t in 1:nt) {
    for (i in 1:ni) {
      for(j in 1:nj) {
        # matching depth layer
        k <- unlist(rhowhich[i, j, t])
        # depth of isopycnal
        z[i,j,t] <- dvals[k]
        # temperature of isopycnal
        d[i, j, t] <- thetao[i, j, k, t]
      }
    }
  }
  toc()
  toc()
  # format into a raster?
  if(rast){
    rdl <- map(1:nt, \(x) {
      di <- d[,,x]
      t(di)[rev(seq_len(nj)),] |> 
      rast(
        extent = rext,
        crs = "EPSG:4326")
    })
    rzl <- map(1:nt, \(x) {
      zi <- z[,,x]
      t(zi)[rev(seq_len(nj)),] |> 
      rast(
        extent = rext,
        crs = "EPSG:4326")
      })
    rd <- rast(rdl)
    names(rd) <- paste0(yr,"_",1:nt)
    rz <- rast(rzl)
    names(rz) <- paste0(yr,"_",1:nt)
    return(list("temp"=rd,"depth"=rz))
    
  } else return(list("temp"=d,"depth"=z))
}
calc_isopyc_yr <- insistently(calc_isopyc_yr,rate = rate_delay(pause=5,max_times=10))
```

```{r}
iso26.5 <- calc_isopyc_yr(ncurl=url,yr=2001,target_rho=1026.5,min_zind=1,max_zind=32,rast=T)
iso25.5 <- calc_isopyc_yr(ncurl=url,yr=2001,target_rho=1025.5,min_zind=1,max_zind=32,rast=T)
```

## Calculate Anomalies

```{r}
isopt <- rast(here('output','isopycnal_1026.5_temp.tif'))
isopz <- rast(here('output','isopycnal_1026.5_depth.tif'))
```

Calculate a monthly climatology.

```{r}
isopt_clim <- tapp(isopt,index='months',fun=mean)
isopz_clim <- tapp(isopz,index='months',fun=mean)
panel(isopt_clim,col=map.pal("magma"))
panel(isopz_clim,col=map.pal("viridis"))
```

Try counting anomalies from these climatologies

```{r}
paldiv <- diverging_hcl(n = 50,h2=0,palette = "Blue Red 2")
paldiv2 <- divergingx_hcl(n= 50,h2=0,palette="Cividis")
```

```{r}
# split into months, subtract climatology, recombine
anomt <- isopt - isopt_clim
anomz <- isopz - isopz_clim

names(anomt) <- time(anomt)
names(anomz) <- time(anomz)

ggplot()+
  geom_spatraster(data=anomt[[270]])+
  scale_fill_continuous(palette=paldiv)+
  labs(title="1026.5 isopycnal",
       fill='temperature (anomaly)')
ggplot()+
  geom_spatraster(data=anomz[[270]])+
  scale_fill_continuous(palette=paldiv2)+
  labs(title="Depth of 1026.5 isopycnal",
       fill='Depth (anomaly)')
```

## Anomaly timeseries

Can we use this dataset to calculate a timeseries? First, a simple mean anomaly over time

```{r}
anomt_ts <- global(anomt,c("mean","sd"),na.rm=T) |> bind_cols(timetbl) |> 
  mutate(upr=mean+1.96*sd,lwr=mean-1.96*sd)
anomz_ts <- global(anomz,c("mean","sd"),na.rm=T) |> bind_cols(timetbl) |> 
  mutate(upr=mean+1.96*sd,lwr=mean-1.96*sd)
# and just normal depth
z_ts <- global(isopz,c("mean","sd"),na.rm=T) |> bind_cols(timetbl) |> 
  mutate(upr=mean+1.96*sd,lwr=mean-1.96*sd)

p_anomt_ts <- anomt_ts |> 
  filter(year<2025) |> 
  ggplot(aes(date,mean,ymin=lwr,ymax=upr))+
  geom_ribbon(fill=viridis_pal()(10)[4],col=NA)+
  geom_line()+
  geom_hline(yintercept=0,linetype=2)+
  scale_x_date(date_breaks="2 years",date_labels="%Y")+
  labs(x="Year",y="Mean Temperature Anomaly\non the 1025.5 isopycnal")
p_anomt_ts

p_anomz_ts <- anomz_ts |> 
  ggplot(aes(date,mean,ymin=lwr,ymax=upr))+
  geom_ribbon(fill=viridis_pal()(10)[4],col=NA)+
  geom_line()+
  geom_hline(yintercept=0,linetype=2)+
  scale_x_date(date_breaks="2 years",date_labels="%Y")+
  labs(x="Year",y="Mean Depth Anomaly\nof the 1025.5 isopycnal")
p_anomz_ts

p_z_ts <- z_ts |> 
  filter(year<2025) |> 
  ggplot(aes(date,mean,ymin=lwr,ymax=upr))+
  geom_ribbon(fill=viridis_pal()(10)[4],col=NA)+
  geom_line()+
  geom_hline(yintercept=0,linetype=2)+
  scale_x_date(date_breaks="2 years",date_labels="%Y")+
  labs(x="Year",y="Mean Depth \nnof the 1025.5 isopycnal")
p_z_ts
```

Try to make a timeseries by latitude bins
```{r}
# make latitude bin raster
lat_rast <- anomt[[1]]  # Get one layer as template
values(lat_rast) <- NA
# Fill with latitude bin IDs
lat_breaks <- seq(32, 50, by=2)  # 2° bins
zonetbl <- tibble(minlat=lat_breaks,maxlat=lead(lat_breaks)) |> 
                    mutate(zone=row_number())

for (i in 1:nrow(lat_rast)) {
  cell_lat <- yFromCell(lat_rast, cellFromRowCol(lat_rast, i,1))
  bin_id <- cut(cell_lat, breaks=lat_breaks, labels=FALSE)
  lat_rast[i, ] <- bin_id
}

# Now use zonal to get mean temperature per bin per time layer
ts_by_lat <- imap(1:nlyr(anomt), \(t,n) {
  ldf <- zonal(anomt[[t]], lat_rast, fun="mean",na.rm=T, as.data.frame=TRUE)
  sddf <- zonal(anomt[[t]], lat_rast, fun="mean",na.rm=T, as.data.frame=TRUE)
  q05df <- zonal(anomt[[t]], lat_rast, fun="quantile",probs=c(0.05),na.rm=T, as.data.frame=TRUE)
  q95df <- zonal(anomt[[t]], lat_rast, fun="quantile",probs=c(0.95),na.rm=T, as.data.frame=TRUE)
  tibble(date=n,zone=ldf[,1],
         mean=ldf[,2],
         sd=sddf[,2],
         q05=q05df[,2],
         q95=q95df[,2])
}) |> bind_rows()

```

```{r}
p_ts_by_lat <- ts_by_lat |> 
  mutate(date=timetbl$date[date]) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x=date,color=as.factor(zone)))+
  geom_line(aes(y=mean))+
  # geom_line(aes(y=q05))+
  # geom_line(aes(y=q95))+
  labs(x="Date",y="Temperature Anomaly",color="Latitude\nBin")
p_ts_by_lat

# compare, e.g., around the southern california bight, around cape blanco, and around cape flaherty
p_ts_by_lat2 <- ts_by_lat |>
  filter(zone %in% c(1,6,9)) |> 
  mutate(date=timetbl$date[date]) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x=date,color=as.factor(zone)))+
  geom_line(aes(y=mean))+
  # geom_line(aes(y=q05))+
  # geom_line(aes(y=q95))+
  labs(x="Date",y="Temperature Anomaly",color="Latitude\nBin")
p_ts_by_lat2
```

## Heatwave Area

```{r}
# use terra::patches to measure areas of features
# for now, define heatwave as temperature > 1 deg above mean
# project to equal area
anomtproj <- project(anomt,"EPSG:5070")
rarea <- cellSize(anomtproj)/1e6

calc_heatwave_area <- function(r){
  # find the area of all cells in heatwave
  rna <- ifel(r<1,NA,r)
  out <- mask(rarea,rna)
  global(out,sum,na.rm=T)
}
```

```{r}
# apply to our raster
heatwave_area_ts <- sapply(anomtproj,calc_heatwave_area)
heatwave_area_ts_df <- tibble(date=timetbl$date,area=unlist(heatwave_area_ts)) |> 
  mutate(area=coalesce(area,0)) |> 
  mutate(doy=yday(date),year=year(date))
p_hw_area <- heatwave_area_ts_df |>
  filter(year %in% c(1997,2014,2019,2020,2022,2023,2024,2025)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(doy,area,color=factor(year)))+geom_line()
p_hw_area
```

```{r}
maker <- function(m){
  t(m)[rev(seq_len(dim(m)[2])),] |> 
      rast(
        extent = rext,
        crs = "EPSG:4326")
}
```
